front: Why RAG instead of fine-tuning on documents?
back: Cheaper, updated in minutes, shows which source was used, model unchanged. Fine-tuning goes stale and gives no attribution.
Offline: clean, chunk, embed, index. Online: embed question, retrieve top-k, (rerank), build prompt with passages, generate.
$\cos(a,b)=a^\top b/(\lVert a\rVert\lVert b\rVert)$: compares direction, ignores length.

front: Unit vectors: cosine = dot = L2 ranking
back: For $\lVert a\rVert=\lVert b\rVert=1$: $\lVert a-b\rVert^2=2-2a^\top b$, so all three order documents identically.
Term count times inverse document frequency $\ln\frac{1+N}{1+df}+1$, then L2-normalised: rare words weigh more.
TF-IDF-like score with saturating term frequency ($k_1$) and document-length normalisation ($b$). Defaults $k_1=1.2$, $b=0.75$.
BM25: exact tokens, great for codes and names, blind to synonyms. Dense: matches meaning, may blur exact strings.
$\text{RRF}(d)=\sum_R 1/(k+\text{rank}_R(d))$, $k\approx60$. Uses ranks only, so no score calibration is needed.

front: Why the constant k in RRF?
back: It flattens the top of the curve so one first place does not outweigh agreement across several lists.
Bi-encoder: separate embeddings, precomputable, fast. Cross-encoder: reads query and document jointly, more accurate, one call per candidate.
Cheap retriever returns ~100 candidates, expensive reranker re-scores them and keeps ~10.
Small chunks lose context; large chunks blur the embedding and waste prompt budget. Overlap protects sentences cut at boundaries.
Cluster vectors with k-means; at query time scan only the nprobe clusters closest to the query. More nprobe = higher recall, slower.
Layered proximity graph: sparse top layers for long jumps, dense bottom layer for fine search; greedy descent gives approximate neighbours in ~log n.

front: Why must query and chunks use the same embedder?
back: Vectors from different models live in different spaces; similarities between them are meaningless.
Fraction of the true (exact) top-k neighbours that the approximate search returns. Measure it against brute force.
